speaker_role: former admissions officer (former director of admissions at Swarthmore College; longtime admissions officer at Vanderbilt University)
commercial_incentive: Briefly promotes a new paid 'Junior Application Materials Review Service' he now offers, at the end of the video.
key_insights: Standardized tests measure reading, math, and language mechanics rather than intelligence, and exist to create a common data point across schools with wildly different grading standards.

At selective colleges, academics (transcript rigor, grades/trends, test scores) function as a threshold to clear, not the deciding factor; once cleared, essays, recommendations, activities, and fit drive decisions.

Describes personally building Swarthmore's test-optional policy during COVID: staff fully hand-redacted all trace of scores from files, including old score reports on transcripts, because partial redaction creates inconsistent, biased evaluation.
Advises comparing your score to a college's Common Data Set middle-50% range for enrolled (not admitted) students, noting admitted-student ranges typically run 40-50 points higher.
Recommends submitting scores only if above the median (especially top 25%), withholding if below median, and using judgment if right at the median.
Notes colleges generally try to protect or raise average test scores except for high institutional priorities like rare talent, athletic recruiting, or major donor/legacy connections.

Contextualized review (family income, first-gen status, rural/urban setting, school resources) happens even where testing is required, and strong AP/IB scores can still reinforce an application submitted test-optional.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker says Swarthmore's test-optional goal was proportional submission, e.g., if 40% of applicants submitted scores, roughly 40% of admits should have too.
Speaker recalls the Democratic Republic of Congo having only one SAT testing center for a population of 119 million.
Speaker says admitted-student test ranges typically run 40-50 points above a college's Common Data Set enrolled-student ranges.
notable_or_distinctive: First-hand, granular account of how one selective college physically redacted test scores from application files to build a genuinely blind test-optional review process.
reliability_notes: Credible former-insider account but self-reported and unverifiable in detail; ends with a pitch for his own paid consulting service, a mild conflict of interest worth noting.
